lxc_7e07635a4ed126d3.text: Meet gelato, baklava, mochi, churros, and alfajores.

lxc_4a71b2f07c3cd267.text: Compare their ingredients, forms, cooking methods, and textures.

lxc_f3efeb1e49797f9b.text: We can ask four questions about a sweet.

lxc_57c4e4332f541361.text: What is its texture, or how does it feel in your mouth?

lxc_a0e1a9a76488e241.text: Gelato is a popular frozen sweet from Italy.

lxc_73ebd9ff39a739d7.text: Its main ingredients are milk, sugar, and flavour.

lxc_e4af12dad0061624.text: Gelato has less air than ice cream, so it is denser.

lxc_288484306211dbff.text: Dense food is closely packed, not light and full of air.

lxc_1c03982bd519ef36.text: Baklava is a popular pastry sweet in Turkey and nearby countries.

lxc_9d9e4d3c2a233105.text: It has many thin layers of pastry with chopped nuts between them.

lxc_15378e1d359d3396.text: Honey or sweet syrup goes over the pastry and soaks into it.

lxc_326c12b6c69e37dd.text: “Soaks into” means the liquid enters the food.

lxc_add48caa79bac73f.text: Baklava and gelato have very different forms.

lxc_1ff4f46a0018ca70.text: Baklava is built from many pastry layers, nuts, and sweet liquid.

lxc_e37d1811cb09e646.text: Mochi is a popular rice cake from Japan.

lxc_82654ef058e4efd4.text: It is made from sticky rice.

lxc_7b8e49ed1f93822c.text: People pound the rice, or hit it again and again, until it becomes soft and stretchy.

lxc_e94ea7cfcfabb09d.text: Mochi has a chewy texture, so you must move your teeth many times when you eat it.

lxc_c058e8e740d7391c.text: Some mochi has sweet bean paste inside.

lxc_cddab6c4a379da27.text: People can also eat it with other sweet toppings.

lxc_82146669227b98a4.text: Unlike layered baklava, mochi is a soft rice cake.

lxc_b135b4efc2c57426.text: A churro is a popular fried dough sweet from Spain.

lxc_eb1a3f3bd3b318ec.text: Frying means cooking food in hot oil.

lxc_a820be126f9b86af.text: The dough cooks until it is golden.

lxc_61880bafd59a6ed5.text: People often roll the churro in sugar after frying it.

lxc_4d6be88cab1b42ec.text: Churros are also eaten in Latin America.

lxc_3217692038d944d3.text: Some people eat them with thick hot chocolate.

lxc_3e06cf3c7e98a41e.text: Their cooking method is different from gelato: churros go into hot oil, but gelato is frozen.

lxc_6777694c85fdf505.text: An alfajor is a popular sweet in Argentina and other parts of South America.

lxc_9c61454f0648dec2.text: Here, “sandwich” means that two round cookies hold a filling in the middle.

lxc_062f4b72540b23dc.text: The filling is a sweet milk caramel.

lxc_24cc2e4d9aa3a7e6.text: Some alfajores also have chocolate or sugar on the outside.

lxc_4ed8f88493632a3e.text: Their form is different from baklava: an alfajor has two cookies around one centre, while baklava has many thin pastry layers.

lxc_baf4213b40222403.text: Gelato is a dense, frozen milk sweet.

lxc_bcef758ceafb948d.text: Baklava is layered pastry with nuts and syrup.

lxc_7a2ea6043c41efd0.text: Mochi is a chewy rice cake.

lxc_da12857b10ca0c56.text: A churro is fried dough, often with sugar.

lxc_d6dbb4b05759b8e1.text: An alfajor is a sandwich cookie with milk caramel.

lxc_fb0fab48628f07c4.text: Their ingredients, forms, cooking methods, and textures make them different.

lxc_cde4926c88e32446.text: One is frozen, one has many layers, one is chewy, one is fried, and one has two cookies around a filling.
